newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hoogovens profits rise, but fall short of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens profits rise, but fall short of forecasts.

text.p: Dutch metals company Hoogovens NV Wednesday reported a 40 percent jump in earnings for the first half of 1997, but the results fell just short of industry analysts' expectations.

The steel and aluminum producer said its net profits rose to 194 million guilders ($91.7 million), from 139 million ($65.8 million) in the same period of 1996, but the results included 13 million guilders ($6.15 million) of extraordinary income from the sale of various small businesses.
Net profits from normal operations rose 25 percent to 178 million guilders ($84.2 million), slightly lower than the average estimate of 186 million guilders ($88 million) forecast by analysts.
Hoogovens said the nascent economic recovery in Europe and favourable conditions elsewhere had led to good demand for its products, allowing it to maintain high sales volumes.
Steel and aluminum prices were even with or slightly lower than first-half 1996 levels, but Hoogovens said it boosted profits by reducing costs and upgrading its product mix.

Hoogovens Chairman Maarten van Veen was optimistic about the outlook for the rest of the year. "The positive performance of the economy will be sustained in the second half of the year, thereby creating room for an increase in prices," he told a news conference.
The company also said the stronger dollar had boosted operating profits by several tens of millions of guilders.

Analysts said the results were somewhat disappointing. "We had thought the result would be more positive than it was," said Kim Broekhuyse of ING Barings. "The quality does not look so good but it's a bit early to tell."
